A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAPSS by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SEBASS evaluations of PS and PM, including correlations with human ratings, encoder analyses, temporal robustness and uncertainty estimates.

after.justification: v2 retains original SEBASS analyses and reports revised music correlations, layer analyses and normalized mutual information results.

M1.justification: The music encoding component changes from AST to MERT (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 4). The distortion bank, diffusion-map procedure, Mahalanobis-based PS, Gamma-tail PM and aggregation formulas remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SEBASS English and Spanish speaker pairs and three-source music mixtures with and without drums. The same temporal-misalignment scenarios remain; no dataset or task is added.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains all 14 competing metrics and both waveform-only variants. SpeechBERT becomes SpeechBERTscore, with identical scores and matching discussion already in v1; this is a naming/citation correction rather than an added comparator.

E3.justification: Music settings change: selected layers become 1 and 3 instead of 2 and 6 for drums and no-drums, and drum-mixture alpha changes from 0 to 1. NMI music frame totals change from 31,965/104,058 to 34,688/66,528. Zero-shot evaluation and PCC/SRCC remain.

E4.justification: Figure 6 revises the music layer-sensitivity analysis for MERT, and the NMI analysis receives revised music curves and frame counts. These address existing questions; the temporal-delay plots, English encoder ablations, uncertainty histograms and English case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain dependence-adjusted sample sizes, 10,000 Monte Carlo draws for SRCC uncertainty, and the same confidence-reporting procedures. v2 Table 2 reproduces the uncertainty values in v1 Table 5; no new seed or repeated-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: Music results are revised under changed settings. For example, drums PM SRCC changes from 67.35% to 75.18%, while PCC changes from 73.33% to 69.88% (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 1). Music layer trends and NMI results also change, with reported maximum NMI falling from about 0.20 to 0.15. Speech and comparator scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The detailed proofs largely carry over into v2 Appendices D–F. However, v2 Eq. 11 changes the truncation limit from N−1 to N despite defining only N−1 nontrivial eigenvalues. Its new Eq. 27 subtracts a squared distance where v1 Eq. 86 and retained v2 Eq. 94 subtract an unsquared distance, introducing mathematical inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The central contributions—complementary PS/PM measures and uncertainty bounds—remain. The claimed temporal resolution changes from the introduction's 50/10 frames per second for speech/music to a maximum of 75. v2 also removes v1's concluding claim that mutual information increases as separation quality deteriorates, which contradicted its results discussion.

C2.justification: The music-layer explanation changes from AST's intermediate-layer vulnerability to MERT's broadly stable representations. The AST-specific explanation for delay robustness is removed, and Appendix G.2 adds a rationale for catalyzing annotated datasets. Existing dataset, aggregation, runtime and problematic-PM-bound limitations remain in G.1.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit distortion-count and retained-dimension ranges, frame lengths and feature dimensions, and supplies the MERT checkpoint. Its new reproducibility statement describes supplementary ZIP code covering inference and bounds. The public code link and hardware/runtime disclosure remain; the ZIP's availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the SpeechBERT/Tseng citation with SpeechBERTScore/Saeki and AST/Gong with MERT/Li. It adds limited references supporting diffusion thresholding, Gamma functions, reverberation and regularization, and removes Hansen–Kollmeier. The central novelty positioning remains, with an added dataset-catalyst discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and main narrative are substantially condensed and reorganized. Diffusion foundations, measure definitions and error guarantees become separate main sections; extensive experimental detail moves to Appendices B–C and limitations to G.1. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: Most experimental displays move into appendices, the original cluster illustration and parameter-summary table disappear, and NMI becomes a redesigned main-text Figure 1. Four uncertainty subtables merge into one wide table. Numerous captions and table layouts change alongside this substantial redistribution.

improvement.justification: The condensed organization, corrected comparator attribution and additional reproducibility details help readers. However, v2 introduces mathematical inconsistencies in Eqs. 11 and 27 while retaining the earlier appendix formulations. Revised music scores use different settings and do not establish a controlled improvement. The balance between better exposition/documentation and reduced mathematical consistency leaves the net quality change unclear.
